summary_md: **Abdullah ([@ikkistan](https://x.com/ikkistan/status/2116740334478876701))** built **agent-readiness**, an open MIT skill that scores a repo's readiness for coding agents across 93 checks in 9 pillars on Factory's five-level Agent Readiness model; a script gathers evidence, the agent judges, and the output is one HTML report (FastAPI scores Level 2) with guided fixes, working in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others ([Luminary-AI-Solutions/agent-readiness](https://github.com/Luminary-AI-Solutions/agent-readiness)). His thread explains that agent failures in his production repos were fixed by fast local hooks, runnable AGENTS.md commands, real-browser E2E and per-session worktrees and ports.

INTRODUCING
Is your repo ready for coding agents?
agent-readiness — An open Agent Skill. Free, MIT.
Five levels: L1 Functional · L2 Documented · L3 Standardized (you are here) · L4 Optimized · L5 Autonomous
93 checks · 9 pillars
Scores your codebase the way an agent experiences it: feedback loops, docs, environment, guardrails. Then helps you fix it, your way.
Each ring a pillar. Red arcs are the gaps.
Claude Code · Codex · Cursor · Copilot · Antigravity · OpenCode · Cline · Droid
npx skills add Luminary-AI-Solutions/agent-readiness

media.description: agent-readiness slide "What it measures": five gated levels and nine pillars (style, build, testing, documentation, dev environment, observability, security, task discovery, product).
agent-readiness slide "How it works": scan, judge, score, show, citing research that LLM-written AGENTS.md raised cost about 20% and agents declared work done too early.
agent-readiness HTML dashboard showing level staircase, a gap map of failing checks and where to start.
agent-readiness slide "Fix it your way": auto-fix, your call and manual lanes.
